content:
We’re happy to share our new paper from FAIR at Meta: WybeCoder.

Verified imperative code generation has long felt just beyond reach, and WybeCoder is a concrete step toward changing that: our system verifies Heapsort using 357 sub-agents and reaches 74% on Verina and 62% on Clever at moderate compute budgets.

WybeCoder works in the Loom/Velvet framework, where VC generation is handled automatically, routine goals are discharged by CVC5 via lean-auto and/or grind, and LLM sub-agents use Lean feedback to tackle the remaining obligations. Beyond pass/fail feedback, sub-agents can suggest updates to both the implementation and its ghost code, such as adding or removing loop invariants.

Code, experiments, and the trajectory viewer are all made available at the links below (CC-BY-NC). We’d love to see the community check it out, get inspired, and build on top of it.

Joint work with @Fabian Glöckle, @Darius Feher , @Kunhao Zheng , @Amaury Hayat , Sean Holden, Gabriel Synnaeve, and Peter O'Hearn.

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29088
Code: https://github.com/facebookresearch/wybecoder
Project page: https://facebookresearch.github.io/wybecoder/
